description:
Russell's guest detailed how the Biden administration worked directly with big tech companies to silence dissenting voices, pointing to a specific American and British organization functioning as the ideological engine behind mass censorship. He described a 2021 report claiming just twelve people, including a well known public figure, were responsible for the majority of anti vaccine sentiment online, and revealed leaked files showing the same organization's top priority was killing off a major social media platform through coordinated advertising boycotts. Russell listened as the guest laid out the evidence, framing it as fear of the truth dressed up as concern over disinformation. Sometimes the people claiming to fight lies are the ones with the most to hide.

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell reacted to reports that outdoor field trials dimming sunlight, potentially through injecting aerosols into the atmosphere, could be approved by the government within weeks. He admitted he doesn't know enough about ecology to say for certain how much human industry is impacting the environment, but he was far more certain about something else entirely. Russell argued that anyone claiming they can help you by literally blocking out the sun is operating from a place that has nothing to do with genuine care for humanity. Some solutions sound so extreme they answer their own question.

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell reacted to a viral video appearing to show a world leader's wife shoving his face as the couple prepared to exit a plane, and the bizarre official response that followed. A source close to the president's office dismissed it as a moment of playful togetherness, unwinding after a long trip. Russell couldn't resist pointing out the absurdity of calling it togetherness, joking that nothing quite says a loving relationship like getting smacked on an airplane. Sometimes the spin is funnier than the incident itself.

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell pointed out a growing gap between what was campaigned on and what's actually unfolding, from renewed involvement near Israel and a likely conflict with Iran to an ongoing war between Russia and Ukraine that was once promised to end almost immediately. He argued none of this was explicitly what was promised, and that the rhetoric never quite matched the reality once in power. Russell fell back on an old piece of wisdom instead, don't follow leaders, watch your own parking meters, because institutions and systems of power are fallible by nature no matter who's running them. Promises are easy to make from the outside looking in.

title: What they're planning next...

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell warned that AI and robotics could make fifty to sixty percent of the population functionally unnecessary under a mass centralized model, a stark contrast to a decentralized world that still needs people to grow food, run communities, teach children, and work in hospitals. He argued the same centralized system driving this shift is deeply entangled with global corporate projects actively destroying the planet. Russell framed it as a spiritual battle as much as an economic one, arguing that the only real power capable of standing against that kind of system isn't political or technological at all. Sometimes the answer to being made redundant isn't resistance, it's remembering what actually can't be automated.

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell's guest opened by framing the Covid crisis as a biological sequel to 9/11, arguing that just as the Patriot Act ushered in mass surveillance after that event, the pandemic ushered in a new era of biosecurity and citizen compliance. He pointed out that the infection fatality ratio was comparable to a severe flu season, yet novel mRNA technology, originally developed through Pentagon research, was rushed to market anyway. Russell responded by acknowledging how difficult it is to prove intent behind events like this, but noted how curious it is that these global crises always seem to benefit the same powerful interests regardless of whether they were deliberately orchestrated. Sometimes the pattern speaks louder than the proof.
